## B — Audience, level and prerequisites: the basics part two: turning, passing, backing, parking and communication
Audience: every first-time Wisconsin Class D applicant, and especially permit holders rehearsing the Y-turn, parking and backing for the skills test.
Why it matters to a first-timer: the chapter gives the Y-turn steps used on the driving exam and the passing and lane-change rules [A04], the hill and parallel parking procedures [A06], and the headlight and signaling thresholds [A08].
Level: procedural sequences plus a handful of exact distances and times; moderate load with several mirror-image rules.
Prerequisites: part one of the basics (right-of-way, speed, space cushions) and the skills test overview in the driving test requirements section.

corpus_stability.reason: The Wisconsin Motorists Handbook prints 2026 on its front cover and form number BDS126 with 2026 on its back cover; it is a yearly-dated handbook with no sign of more than one rewrite per year in the selected pages.
